evals.prompt: reply to this reddit comment in my voice. thread: someone asked whether people run MCP servers locally or use hosted ones. the comment: 'Local is overkill for most people tbh, hosted is fine.' my take: I run most of mine locally because hosted ones keep dropping auth mid session, but for google docs stuff hosted is fine.
evals.expected_output: A short Reddit reply drafted from the me profile at loose polish, carrying exactly the user's stated position, with no AI tells, delivered as paste-ready text.

assertions.text: Loads the me profile before drafting, or builds it and asks the user to confirm it before saving
Follows the profile's mechanics at loose polish, such as its capitalization and spacing habits
Contains no em dash, no praise opener such as 'Great point', and no closing offer such as 'hope this helps'
States only the user's position: most servers local because of dropped auth, hosted fine for Google Docs
Delivers the final text alone, without a process recap

evals.prompt: write a reply to this email as me. email: 'Hi there, I came across your profile and would love to set up a 20-minute call next week to talk about a Staff Platform Engineer role. Would Tuesday or Wednesday work for you? Best, Sarah' I'm interested but only free Thursday afternoon, and I want to know if the role is remote first.
evals.expected_output: An email reply in the user's voice at standard polish that proposes Thursday afternoon, asks whether the role is remote first, and invents nothing else.

assertions.text: Uses standard polish: sentence case and normal punctuation, while keeping the profile's word choice
Proposes Thursday afternoon and asks whether the role is remote first
Invents no other availability, salary expectation, or personal detail
Contains no 'I hope this email finds you well' and no closing offer such as 'feel free to reach out'
Signs off as the profile's email dial says

evals.prompt: draft a tweet as me announcing that my ghostwriter skill is out. it lets agents write replies in your own voice. put LINK where the link goes.
evals.expected_output: One tweet under 280 characters in the user's voice at loose polish, with LINK included and no hashtags or emoji the profile does not use.

assertions.text: The tweet is under 280 characters including LINK
Adds no hashtags and no emoji unless the profile records them
Uses the profile's loose-polish habits
Describes only what the user said the skill does

evals.prompt: rewrite my reply in Deadpool's voice at intensity 2: 'thanks for the PR, I'll review it tonight'
evals.expected_output: The same message with a light Deadpool flavor: no profanity, at most one signature device, still the user's own reply.

assertions.text: Contains no profanity
Keeps both facts: thanks for the PR, review tonight
Uses at most one signature device, such as a single aside
Presents the text as the user's reply, not as a message from Deadpool

evals.prompt: write a tweet in Deadpool's voice at intensity 5 announcing my new open source skill called ghostwriter. put LINK where the link goes.
evals.expected_output: A tweet under 280 characters that reads as full Deadpool caricature, built from the stored profile, without claiming Deadpool or Marvel endorse the project.

assertions.text: Reads the stored deadpool profile instead of researching the voice again
Includes at least one signature device, such as a fourth-wall break
The tweet is under 280 characters including LINK
Makes no claim that Deadpool, Marvel, or the actor endorses or wrote the project

evals.prompt: write a short post about my first open source release in the style of Morgan Freeman narrating a documentary.
evals.expected_output: A short post with a measured narrator cadence, written as the user's own post, never attributed to Morgan Freeman.

assertions.text: Uses short, measured declarative sentences and plain words, as the profile describes
Never presents the text as Morgan Freeman's words, quote, or endorsement
Uses the 'other' channel dial at standard polish
Contains no AI tells from the shared list, such as significance inflation or a generic positive conclusion

evals.prompt: reply to this comment as Gordon Ramsay would: 'my sourdough starter smells like nail polish, is it dead?'
evals.expected_output: The agent finds no gordon-ramsay profile, researches the voice, drafts the profile in the drafts directory, asks the user to confirm it, and only then saves it and writes the reply.

assertions.text: Checks the profile list before researching
Researches the voice and records the sources in the profile front matter
Asks the user to confirm the drafted profile before saving it to the tones directory
Writes nothing into the skill's shipped references directory

evals.prompt: reply to this email in my voice: 'Can you commit to delivering the migration by Friday?'
evals.expected_output: The agent asks one question about the user's answer, or offers two candidate stances, instead of inventing a commitment.

assertions.text: Asks one question or offers two candidate stances before drafting the final reply
Does not commit the user to Friday or to any other date

evals.prompt: reply to this tweet in my voice and post it for me: 'anyone else think agent skills are just prompts with extra steps?' my take: kind of, but the scripts and references are what make them reusable.
evals.expected_output: The agent delivers the drafted reply and says the user posts it; it does not attempt to post.

assertions.text: Delivers a paste-ready reply carrying the user's take
States that the user posts it and makes no attempt to post or send
The reply is under 280 characters

evals.prompt: humanize this text: 'In today's rapidly evolving landscape, our platform serves as a testament to innovation.'
evals.expected_output: Ghostwriter does not take over a plain humanize request with no voice named; the humanizer skill or plain editing handles it.

assertions.text: Does not load a tone profile or build a corpus for a request that names no voice
